name: KridinifyTech SEO Connector for TrendSync
author: kridin1729

sections.description:
KridinifyTech SEO Connector for TrendSync connects your WordPress site to the TrendSync backend API, automatically injecting optimized SEO metadata including:

  • Meta titles and descriptions
  • Open Graph tags for social media sharing
  • Twitter Card tags
  • JSON-LD structured data
  • Canonical URLs
  • Keywords and meta tags

The plugin communicates with your TrendSync backend server to fetch real-time SEO optimizations. This ensures your content is always optimized and search engines are notified of changes immediately.

This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by TrendSync.

Privacy

This plugin connects only to your own configured TrendSync backend server to fetch SEO metadata. No data is sent to any third-party services.

Support

Visit https://kridinifytech.in or email support@kridinifytech.in
sections.installation:
From WordPress.org

  1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New.
  2. Search for “KridinifyTech SEO Connector for TrendSync”.
  3. Click Install Now and then Activate.
  4. Go to Settings → TrendSync.
  5. Enter your API Key, Client ID, Backend URL, and Website URL.
  6. Click Save Settings and then Verify Connection.

Manual Installation

  1. Upload the kridinifytech-seo-connector-for-trendsync folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate via Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings → TrendSync.
  4. Enter your API Key, Client ID, Backend URL, and Website URL.
  5. Click Save Settings and then Verify Connection.
sections.faq:
How do I get an API Key?

Sign up at your TrendSync dashboard and generate an API key from the settings page.

What is the Backend URL?

This is your TrendSync API server URL (e.g., https://api.yourdomain.com).

Does this work with caching plugins?

Yes, but clear your cache after configuration changes. The plugin caches metadata for 10 minutes per page to reduce API calls.

Will this slow down my site?

No. Metadata is cached for 10 minutes per page path, minimizing API calls.

What happens if the backend is unavailable?

The plugin fails gracefully — your site continues to work normally, just without injected metadata.
